In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Commentary on Surah Hud

Surah Hud is Meccan, except for the words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And establish prayer at the two ends of the day and in the first hours of the night﴾ to the end of the verse; for that part is Medinan.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Alif-Lam-Ra﴾. Its meaning is: "I am Allah, the One who sees." And His words: ﴿A Book﴾ mean: this is a Book.

As for His words: ﴿Its verses have been made firm﴾, there are several opinions concerning it:

Qatadah said: its meaning is that Allah has made them firm, so there is in them no contradiction and no inconsistency.

The second: the meaning of His words "its verses have been made firm" is that they are muhkam (firm, clear in meaning), not abrogated (mansukh).

The third: ﴿its verses have been made firm﴾ means: through the command and the prohibition, and the lawful and the unlawful.

As for His words: ﴿then detailed﴾, there are several opinions: the first is that it was detailed through promise and threat. Mujahid said: "fussilat" means it was explained and made clear. The third: "then detailed" means that Allah sent it down piece by piece.

It has also been said: its verses were made firm for those who reflect, then its rulings were detailed for the God-fearing.

It has also been said: its verses were made firm for the hearts, then its rulings were detailed for the bodies.

In a non-canonical reading it is recited: "thumma fussilat," and its meaning is that they came (i.e., "thumma" here indicates the verses came from ...).

﴿From the presence of One who is All-Wise, All-Aware﴾, that is: from the presence of One who is All-Wise, All-Aware.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 2:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿That you worship none but Allah﴾. Concerning it there are two opinions:

One of them: "that" is explanatory, meaning: that you worship none but Allah.

The second opinion: it means "He commands you that you worship none but Allah."

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, I am to you from Him a warner and a bringer of good tidings﴾ means: a warner to the disobedient, and a bringer of good tidings to the obedient.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 3:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And that you seek forgiveness from your Lord, then turn to Him in repentance﴾. The scholars of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) said: He placed forgiveness before repentance only because forgiveness is what is sought through repentance.

In some reports: "Whoever seeks forgiveness does not persist, even if he returns to it seventy times." And in some reports: "There is no minor sin with persistence, and no major sin with seeking forgiveness."

There is another view regarding the verse: that the meaning of His words ﴿And that you seek forgiveness from your Lord﴾ refers to the past, and ﴿then turn to Him﴾ refers to the future.

His words ﴿He will let you enjoy a good provision﴾ mean: He will let you live a good life. It is also said: He will grant you a good lifespan. As for the good life, some of them said: it is contentment with what is readily available and patience with what is decreed. It is also said: the good life is the goodness of the soul and abundance of provision. It is said: the good life is sufficiency through what is lawful. His words ﴿until a specified term﴾ mean: until the time of death.

His words ﴿and He will give every person of merit his merit﴾ have two interpretations. The first: its meaning is that He will give every person of good deeds in this world his reward in the Hereafter.

The second view: His words ﴿He will give every person of merit his merit﴾ mean: whoever acts for the sake of Allah, Allah will grant him success in what is to come in obedience to Him and will guide him to it.

It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he said: Everything a person seeks reward for, whether a word or a deed, is included in this, even a single word he utters.

His words ﴿But if they turn away﴾ mean: if they turn away (in disbelief). His words ﴿Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a great day﴾ mean: the Day of Resurrection.
Then God Most High said: ﴿To God is your return, and He is over all things competent.﴾ The meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 5:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿Verily they fold up their breasts to hide from Him﴾, and the rest of the verse. ʿAbd Allah ibn Shaddad said: A disbelieving man would pass by the Prophet, fold his chest, and cover himself with his garment out of hatred for the Prophet, so that the Prophet would not see him and he would not see the Prophet. And from some of them: a man from among the disbelievers would enter his house, let down his curtain, cover himself with his garment, bend his back, and say: "Does God know what is in my heart?" And from Abu Razin, something close to the first statement. Then God the Exalted revealed this verse.

As for the meaning of His words ﴿they fold up their breasts﴾: that is, they bend and fold (themselves). From this comes the expression thanaya al-thawb (he folded the garment). A poet used the word for covering oneself:

(I tend the stars, though I was not ordered to tend them... and at times I cover myself with the surplus of my rags.)

As for His words ﴿to hide from Him﴾: that is, to hide from God the Exalted. It has also been said: to hide from the Prophet.

In the irregular reading (al-shadh) it is related that Ibn ʿAbbas, may God be pleased with them both, recited: "Verily they fold (yathnuwni) their breasts," on the pattern of yafʿawʿil, as one says yuhlawli (it is sweet to me).

﴿Yet when they cover themselves with their garments﴾: meaning, they cover themselves with their garments. The words of the Exalted: {He knows what they conceal and what they reveal; indeed He is Knower of what is in the breasts}. Al-Azhari and others said: the meaning of the verse from its beginning to its end is: those who harbour enmity toward the Prophet, their condition is not hidden from us. In some tafsir works it is stated: a man who concealed enmity toward the Prophet used to visit him and show love for him, so God the Exalted revealed this verse concerning him.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 6:

His words, the Exalted: ﴿And there is no creature on the earth but that upon Allah is its provision﴾, to the end of the verse. Al-dabbah (the creeping creature): every living being that crawls upon the earth. His words ﴿but that upon Allah is its provision﴾ mean: indeed Allah makes its provision a means and facilitates it.

The scholars of ma'ani (the science of the meanings of the Qur'an) said: this is subject to His will, because He may provide and He may not provide. As for His words ﴿and He knows its place of rest and its place of storage﴾, there are several opinions regarding this verse:

Muqatil reported from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: al-mustaqarr (the place of rest) is the place where it takes shelter, and al-mustawda' (the place of storage) is the place where it is buried.

And from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: al-mustaqarr is the wombs of the mothers, and al-mustawda' is the place where it is buried.

Some of them said: al-mustaqarr is that upon which its deeds settle, and al-mustawda' is that to which its affair returns in the end.

It is also said: al-mustaqarr is the wombs of the mothers, and al-mustawda' is the loins of the fathers. This is also narrated from Ibn 'Abbas.

As for His words ﴿all in a clear Book﴾, it refers to the Preserved Tablet.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 7:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿It is He who created the heavens and the earth in six days﴾. We have explained this before.

And His words: ﴿And His Throne was upon the water﴾. Ibn ʿAbbas said: "The Throne was upon the water, and the water was upon the back of the wind," meaning: the solid part of the wind. Yazid ibn Harun narrated from Hammad ibn Salamah, from Waki ibn Hudus, from Abu Razin al-ʿUqayli that he said: "O Messenger of Allah, where was our Lord before He created His creation?" He said: "In ʿama (a cloud or mist), above it was air and below it was air, and His Throne was upon the water." Yazid ibn Harun said: the meaning of His words "in ʿama" is: there was nothing with Him besides Him. Abu ʿIsa (al-Tirmidhi) related it in his book in this manner.

His words: ﴿That He may test you, which of you is best in deed﴾. Its meaning: that He may test you, which of you is most obedient to Allah the Exalted, most swift to seek the pleasure of Allah, and most scrupulous in refraining from the things Allah has forbidden. Its meaning: testing from Allah. We have explained this before.

And His words: ﴿And if you say, "Indeed you will be resurrected after death," those who disbelieve will surely say, "This is not but obvious magic."﴾ Meaning: this is nothing but manifest deception.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 8:

The Exalted's saying: ﴿And if We defer the punishment from them until a counted community﴾ means: until a counted term (ajal ma'dudah).

His saying: ﴿they will surely say, "What is holding it back?"﴾ means: those who disbelieved will surely say: "What thing is holding it back?" That is, the punishment.

His saying: ﴿Unquestionably, on the day it comes to them, it will not be averted from them﴾ means: unquestionably, on the day the punishment comes to them, the punishment will not be averted from them.

His saying: ﴿And there will befall them what they used to mock﴾ means: there will descend upon them the recompense of their mockery.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 9:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if We let man taste mercy from Us﴾. Here "mercy" (al-rahmah) means abundance of provision.

And His saying: ﴿Then We withdraw it from him﴾, meaning, We take it away from him. His saying: ﴿Indeed, he is despairing and ungrateful﴾, i.e., despairing of the mercy of God, may He be exalted, ungrateful for the blessing of God.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 10:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And if We let him taste ease after hardship has touched him, he will surely say, "The bad times have left me." Indeed, he is exultant and boastful.﴾ That is, the human being says, "The bad times have left me," by his own deserving of it, and does not see it as coming from God, exalted is He.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, he is exultant and boastful.﴾ Al-farah (exultation): a pleasure in the heart at attaining what one desires. Al-fakhr (boasting): is belittling people by enumerating one's virtues, and it is forbidden in the Qur'an in many places.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 11:

And His saying: ﴿Except those who are patient﴾. Al-Farra' (al-Farra') and al-Zajjaj (al-Zajjaj) said: this is an exceptive (istithna') that is disjunctive (munqati'), and its meaning is: "But those who are patient (sabaru) ﴿and do righteous deeds—those will have forgiveness and a great reward﴾." Its meaning is evident.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 12:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Perhaps you would leave out part of what is revealed to you and your breast would be constricted by it﴾. The people of tafsir (exegesis) said: The occasion of revelation of the verse is that when the disbelievers said, "O Muhammad, bring a Qur'an other than this, or change it," meaning: bring a Qur'an in which there is no reviling of our gods, as we mentioned in the surah of Yunus, the Prophet resolved to leave off openly reviling their gods. So God, exalted is He, sent down this verse: ﴿Perhaps you would leave out part of what is revealed to you﴾, meaning: the reviling of the gods openly, ﴿and your breast would be constricted by it﴾, meaning: and perhaps your breast would be constricted ﴿lest they say, "Why has not a treasure been sent down to him or an angel come with him?"﴾, meaning: why has a treasure not been sent down to him or an angel not come with him. His saying: ﴿You are only a warner﴾, its meaning: upon you is only the warning and the conveyance (of the message), and it is not upon you to bring the signs that they propose.

And His saying ﴿And Allah is Disposer of all things﴾, meaning: Guardian (ḥafīẓ).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 13:

The words of His, exalted is He: ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"?﴾ mean: "Rather, they say, 'He has invented it.'" Iftarahu (he invented it) means ikhtalaqahu (he fabricated it). ﴿Say: "Then bring ten surahs like it, invented."﴾ And the meaning of "like it" is: like it in eloquence (balaghah).

Ali ibn Isa al-Nahwi (the grammarian) said: Eloquence has three levels. The highest level is miraculous (mu'jizah), and the middle and lowest levels are attainable. The Qur'an is at the highest level of eloquence.

If it is said: He said in Surah Yunus: ﴿Then bring a surah like it﴾, and they were unable to bring a surah. How then is it valid for Him to say to them: ﴿Then bring ten surahs like it﴾? This is only like a man who says to another, "Give me a dirham," and the other is unable to, so he says, "Give me ten dirhams." Also, He said: ﴿invented﴾, and can it be permissible for God, exalted is He, to command them to bring forth fabrication?

The answer to this: Among them are those who said: Surah Hud was revealed first, although in the arrangement it is later. Al-Mubarrad rejected this and said: No, rather Surah Yunus was revealed first. He answered the question and said: The meaning of His words ﴿then bring a surah like it﴾ in Surah Yunus is: like it in the report of the unseen and the rulings, and the promise and the warning. So they were unable. Then He said to them in Surah Hud: If you are unable to bring a surah like the Qur'an in its reports, its rulings, its promise and its warning, then bring ten surahs like it, invented, meaning: fabricated, without any report of the unseen, nor any ruling, nor any promise or warning, and they are merely eloquence. And this is a sound answer.

As for the second question, the answer is: We say: God, glorified and exalted is He, did not command them to fabricate, but rather issued a challenge (tahaddi). Its meaning is: your insistence on denying Muhammad and your claim that he invented the Qur'an obliges you to bring something like it by fabrication, so that the lie of Muhammad may become apparent, as you claimed. When you were unable, it showed that he is truthful.

As for His words: ﴿And call upon whomever you can besides God﴾, its meaning is: seek help from whomever you can besides God ﴿if you are truthful﴾.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 14:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And if they do not respond to you, then know that it was revealed with the knowledge of Allah﴾. It is permissible that His words ﴿then know﴾ be addressed to the believers, and it is also permissible that it be addressed to the polytheists. His words ﴿with the knowledge of Allah﴾ mean: He revealed it, and His knowledge is in it. This is a refutation of the Mu'tazilah (al-Mu'tazilah, the rationalist theological school), when they said: "Allah has no knowledge."

And His words: ﴿and that there is no god but Him; so will you be Muslims?﴾ mean: know that there is no god but Him, so will you be Muslims? That is: sincere (mukhlisun, those who are sincere in devotion).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 15:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Whoever desires the life of this world and its adornment, We will pay them in full for their deeds therein﴾. Al-Dahhak said: The verse was revealed concerning the polytheists. Mujahid and a group said: The verse was revealed concerning everyone who performs an action and intends by it other than Allah. As for His words ﴿We will pay them in full for their deeds therein﴾, it means: We will recompense them for their deeds in this world, by abundance of provision, the averting of hardships, and what is similar to that. As for His words ﴿and they therein will not be deprived﴾, "therein" means: in this world; "they will not be deprived" means: their share will not be diminished. Then he said:

Those are the ones for whom there is nothing in the Hereafter but the Fire, and what they did in it has come to nothing (﴿وَحَبِطَ مَا صَنَعُوا فِيهَا﴾). I.e., it became null and void (وَبَطَلَ مَا صَنَعُوا فِيهَا). And His saying: ﴿وَبَاطِلٌ مَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ means: and what they used to do was void (وَمَا حَقَّ مَا كَانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ), that is, it did not stand as true or valid.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 17:

His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿Is one who is upon clear evidence from his Lord﴾. There is an ellipsis in the verse, and its meaning is: Is one who is upon clear evidence from his Lord like one who desires the worldly life and its adornment? Most of the people of tafsir (tafsir, exegesis) hold that what is meant by it is the Prophet. It has been said that what is meant is the Prophet and every believer in the world. The first is the correct view.

His saying: ﴿upon clear evidence from his Lord﴾ means: upon a clarification from his Lord. His saying ﴿and there follows it a witness from Him﴾ has several views:

The first: Most of the people of tafsir hold that what is meant by it is Jibril (peace be upon him). This is the saying of Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Mansur ibn al-Mu'tamir, a student of al-Nakha'i, al-Nakha'i, and others.

The second view: that His saying ﴿and there follows it a witness from Him﴾ means the tongue of Muhammad. This is related from al-Hasan al-Basri, and some have narrated it from [al-Husayn] ibn 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with them both.

The third: that His saying ﴿and there follows it a witness from Him﴾ is 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him. It is narrated from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "There is no man of Quraysh but that a verse of the Qur'an was revealed concerning him." It was said to him: "And was anything revealed concerning you?" He said: ﴿and there follows it a witness from Him﴾.

The fourth: ﴿and there follows it a witness from Him﴾ is an angel from among the angels, who descended to guard him, make him firm, and bear witness for him.

It has been said that His saying ﴿a witness from Him﴾ is the Gospel, and its meaning is: it follows him confirming him, that is, it is confirming him. His saying ﴿and before it was the Book of Musa as a guide﴾ means by it the Torah. His saying ﴿as a guide and a mercy﴾ means that it was a guide and a mercy for whoever followed it, and it confirms the Qur'an and bears witness to the Prophet. His saying ﴿those believe in it﴾: some said it means the Muhajirun and the Ansar. Others said it means those among the People of the Book who embraced Islam. His saying ﴿and whoever disbelieves in it﴾ means: in the Messenger, ﴿among the factions﴾, and they formed factions against the Prophet, that is, they split from their tribes and gathered against him from Quraysh and others. In some tafsirs it is said that they were the Banu Umayyah, the Banu al-Mughirah, and the Banu Abi Talhah ibn 'Abd al-'Uzza, and what is meant is the disbelievers among them, not the Muslims.

The second view concerning the verse: that the factions are all the religious communities. Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him, related that the Prophet said: "No one hears of me and then does not believe, except that Allah will admit him into the Fire." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "I sought the confirmation of this from the Qur'an and found it in His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And whoever disbelieves in it among the factions, the Fire is his promised place﴾."

His saying: ﴿So do not be in doubt about it﴾ means: do not be in doubt about it. It has also been said its meaning is: do not be in any doubt about it, O doubter. His saying: ﴿Indeed it is the truth from your Lord, but most of the people do not believe﴾ is clear in meaning.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 18:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And who is more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah or denies His signs?﴾ Its meaning: there is no one more unjust than one who fabricates a lie against Allah. Then He said: ﴿Those will be presented before their Lord.﴾ The ʿarḍ (presentation, exposure) is the manifestation of a thing so that it is seen and its state is examined, and from it comes their saying: "The sultan reviewed (ʿarada) the troops." And His saying: ﴿And the witnesses will say, "These are the ones who lied against their Lord."﴾ Scholars differed regarding the witnesses (al-ashhād). It is related from Ibn ʿAbbas that he said: they are the prophets and messengers. Mujahid said: they are the angels. Others said: they are all of creation. And His saying: ﴿"Unquestionably, the curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers"﴾ its meaning is apparent.

Ibn ʿUmar (may Allah be pleased with them both) narrated that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "The believer will be brought near to his Lord on the Day of Resurrection until He places His covering (kanaf) over him, and He will make him confess his sins and say: 'Do you know such-and-such?' He will say: 'I know.' 'Do you know such-and-such?' He will say: 'I know.' He will ask him about everything, then He will say: 'I concealed it for you in the world, and I forgive it for you today.' Then his book will be given to him in his right hand. As for the disbelievers, they will be called out before the witnesses: 'These are the ones who lied against their Lord. Unquestionably, the curse of Allah is upon the wrongdoers.'"

This hadith is the hadith of al-najwa (the private conference), and the scholars agreed upon its authenticity from the Prophet (ﷺ).

"The words of the Most High: ﴿Those who bar from the way of Allah﴾ mean: those who hinder [people] from the religion of Allah.

And His words: ﴿and seek to make it crooked﴾ mean: and they seek crookedness in the religion of Allah. And His words {and they, in the Hereafter, they are disbelievers}: Tha'lab said: the repetition of "they" is for emphasis, since the Hereafter has come between the two."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 20:

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿They were not able to escape (mu'jizin) in the earth﴾. Its meaning: they were not those who could get away. It was also said: they were not those who fled from Our punishment, for whoever flees from a thing is overcome by it (al-'ajz 'anhu). His statement: ﴿And they had no protectors apart from Allah﴾ means: no helpers or guardians against Our punishment. His statement: ﴿Their punishment will be doubled﴾. If it is asked: what is the meaning of the doubling of the punishment, when He said elsewhere: ﴿And whoever brings an evil deed, he will not be recompensed except the like of it﴾?

The answer is in two respects:

The first: the doubling of the punishment is due to the doubling of the crime.

The second: the verse concerns the leaders of the people of polytheism, and the doubling of the punishment upon them is due to their misleading of their followers and their calling them to their shirk.

His statement: ﴿They were not able to hear, and they did not see﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: Allah placed a barrier between them and faith. Al-Farra' mentioned from some scholars of meanings (ahl al-ma'ani) that the meaning of the verse is: their punishment is doubled because they were able to hear but did not listen, so they did not listen.

All the other grammarians rejected the assumption of a "ba'" (bi-, "because of") here. Al-istita'ah (capacity, ability) is a power by which the limbs are made obedient for action.

There is a third opinion regarding the verse: that since they did not listen with the listening of understanding (al-tafahhum) and benefiting from it, and did not see with the sight of reality, He made them like one who is unable to hear and see.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 21:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Those are the ones who have lost their souls﴾ mean: they cheated themselves (ghabanu anfusahum). It has also been said that the greatest loss is the loss of the soul, and the greatest gain is the gain of the soul. And His words: ﴿and what they used to invent has forsaken them﴾ mean: what they used to claim of the intercession of the angels and the idols has departed from them and failed them.

**Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 22:**

The words of the Most High: ﴿Without doubt﴾ (lā jarama) have two opinions:

The first: lā jarama means: truly, in truth (ḥaqqan), ﴿that they, in the Hereafter, are the greatest losers﴾.

The second opinion: that His words ﴿lā﴾ ("no") are a rejection of what they said, and His words ﴿jarama﴾ are the beginning of a statement. Jarama here means: he earned (kasaba). The poet said:

(And indeed I struck Abu ʿUyayna a blow, and it earned Fazara, after it, that they became angry.)

That is: it earned them anger. And another said:

(We set up his head on the trunk of a palm, for what his hands had earned (jarrat), and we did not transgress.)

So the meaning of the verse: jarama, that is: earned for them their disbelief, perdition and loss.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 23:

The words of the Most High: ﴿Indeed, those who believe and do righteous deeds and humble themselves before their Lord﴾. Mujahid said: that is, they were humbly submissive (khasha'u). Some of them said: they were at peace and content (ita'mannu). It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: they feared (khafu). And His words ﴿before their Lord﴾ mean: to their Lord, like the words of the Most High ﴿because your Lord has inspired her﴾, meaning: to her. Likewise here: "ila rabbihim" (to their Lord).

And His words ﴿Those are the companions of the Garden; they will abide therein eternally﴾: the meaning is apparent.

The Words of the Exalted: "The likeness of the two parties is like the blind and the deaf, and the seeing and the hearing..." to the end of the verse. The two parties here are: the party of the disbelievers, and the party of the believers. As for His words, "like the blind and the deaf," there are two views on it:

The first: that the "waw" (and) is extra (ṣilah), and its meaning is: like the blind-deaf, just as one says: "I saw the intelligent and the witty," meaning: "I saw the intelligent witty one."

The second view: that the "waw" is for generalizing the comparison, and its meaning is: the state of the disbeliever is like the state of the blind, and his state is like the state of the deaf, and his state is like the state of the blind and the deaf.

As for His words, "and the seeing and the hearing," the discussion regarding it is like this, and what is meant by it is the state of the believer. As for His words, "Are they equal in comparison?" it is narrated that when the disbelievers heard this, they said: "They are not equal." So Allah the Exalted revealed: "Will you not then be mindful?" meaning: Will you not then take admonition?

His saying: ﴿And We certainly sent Noah to his people: "Indeed I am a clear warner to you."﴾ It has been recited in two readings (qira'at): with the naṣb (accusative case) and with the khafḍ (genitive case). The meaning of the naṣb reading is: "bi-annī (بِأَنِّي) lakum nadhīrun mubīn," that is, "that I am a clear warner to you."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 26:

The words of the Exalted: ﴿That you worship none but Allah﴾. Its meaning: "I command you that you worship none but Allah." Worship ('ibadah) here means tawhid (affirmation of God's oneness). He began with tawhid because it is among the most important matters.

And His words: ﴿Indeed, I fear for you the punishment of a painful day﴾. That is: "painful" means causing pain, and the painful is that which is agonizing.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 27:

The saying of the Exalted: ﴿So the chiefs of those among his people who disbelieved said﴾. Al-Mala' (the chiefs) are the nobles and the leaders.

And His saying: ﴿We see you only as a human like ourselves﴾, its meaning is apparent. And His saying: ﴿And we see none following you except those who are the lowest of us, immature in judgment﴾. Al-arādhil (the lowest) is the plural of al-radhl, and al-radhl is the base and worthless. It has been said: al-arādhil are al-asāfil (the lowest), and al-radhl is al-suflah (the riffraff). Regarding al-suflah there are many opinions among the scholars.

Malik ibn Anas said: al-suflah is the one who reviles the Companions of the Prophet.

It is narrated from al-Hasan ibn Ziyad al-Lu'lu'i that he said: al-suflah is the one who has no religion.

And from al-Asma'i that he said: al-suflah is the one who does not care what he says or what is said to him.

And from Ibn al-Mubarak who said: they are those who beg and go to the doors of the judges seeking testimonies.

Tha'lab narrated from Ibn al-A'rabi who said: al-suflah is the one who eats with his religion, and the suflat al-suflah is the one who trades the religion of others for his worldly gain. And in some reports: the most wretched of the wretched is one who sells his religion for the worldly gain of another. It has also been said that al-suflah are the people of base crafts, such as the sweepers, the tanners, the fishmongers, the cuppers, the weavers, and others. It is related that a certain scholar in Baghdad was asked about a woman who said to her husband: "O suflah!" He said: "If I am a suflah, then you are divorced." That scholar said to him: "What is your craft?" He said: "A fishmonger." He said: "A suflah, by God, a suflah."

It is related from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: they are those who, when they gather, prevail, and when they scatter, are not recognized.

And His saying: ﴿immature in judgment﴾ has been recited in two readings: with hamza and without hamza. As for with hamza, its meaning is: the first of the opinion; as if they said: they followed you at first glance without reflecting, and had they reflected, they would not have followed you. As for bādī al-ra'y without hamza, its meaning is: apparent opinion. Al-Zajjaj said: that is, they followed you outwardly, not inwardly.

And His saying: ﴿And we see no merit for you over us; rather, we think you are liars﴾, its meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 28:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿He said, "O my people, tell me: if I were upon clear evidence from my Lord"﴾ means: upon clear proof (bayan) from my Lord. And His words: ﴿and He had given me mercy from Himself﴾ — mercy here is prophethood and guidance. His words ﴿but it has been obscured from you﴾ mean: it has been hidden from you, because whoever is blind to a thing, that thing has been hidden from him. It has been recited as "fa-ʿummiyat ʿalaykum" (ﻓﻌﻤﻴﺖ ﻋﻠﻴﻜﻢ), meaning: "fa-ukhfiyat ʿalaykum" (then it was concealed from you). His words ﴿Shall we compel you to accept it﴾ mean: shall we compel you to accept the call, ﴿while you are averse to it?﴾ Qatadah said: "Had the prophets been able to compel their people, they would have compelled them; but they were not able to."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 29:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And O my people, I do not ask you for wealth in return for it; my reward is only from Allah﴾. Its meaning: my reward is only from Allah.

And His saying: ﴿Nor will I drive away those who have believed﴾. In it is evidence that they (the disbelievers) asked him to drive away the believers.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, they are to meet their Lord﴾, meaning: indeed, they are going to their Lord, and He will recompense the one who drove them away.

And His saying: ﴿But I see you as a people who are ignorant﴾, the meaning is apparent.

Almighty God's words: ﴿O my people, who would protect me from God if I drove them away?﴾ Its meaning: who would prevent me from the punishment of God if I drove them away? ﴿Will you not then take heed?﴾ That is: will you not then admonish yourselves?

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 31:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And I do not say to you, "With me are the treasures of Allah"﴾ means: I do not have the treasures of Allah, so that I could bring you what you seek. And His saying: ﴿Nor do I know the unseen﴾ means: I do not know the unseen so that I could inform you of what you wish. And His saying: ﴿Nor do I say, "Indeed, I am an angel"﴾ is a reply to their saying: ﴿We see you only as a human being like ourselves﴾. And His saying: ﴿Nor do I say to those whom your eyes look down upon [tazdari]﴾ — tazdari means: to despise and regard as worthless. This is a reply to their saying: ﴿And we see not following you except those who are the lowest of us, at first appearance﴾.

As for His saying, ﴿Allah will not give them any good﴾, it means: Allah will not give them any reward. ﴿Allah is most knowing of what is within themselves﴾. [That is: in their breasts, regarding whether Allah will give them good.]

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, I would then be among the wrongdoers﴾ means: indeed, I would then be among the wrongdoers, if I said this or drove them away.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 32:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They said, "O Noah, you have disputed with us and multiplied our disputation."﴾ It is related from Ibn 'Abbas that he read "fa-aktharta jidalana" (فَأَكْثَرت جدالنا) with a fatha. Al-mujadalah (contention, debate) is a dispute carried out with an emphasis on intensity. The origin of jadal (argumentation, contention) is twisting (al-fatl), and the Arabs call the falcon al-ajdal (الأجدل), because of its strength in hunting birds.

The difference between ihtijaj (argument, proof) and mujadalah is that what is sought in ihtijaj is the manifestation of the truth regarding the matter in question, whereas what is sought in mujadalah is the opponent's return to the other party's view.

The difference between mira' (wrangling, doubting dispute) and mujadalah is that mira' is blameworthy, because it is a dispute after the truth has become manifest, whereas jidal is not blameworthy, except when one goes to excess in it without intending to seek the truth.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿So bring us what you threaten us with, if you are among the truthful.﴾ This is evidence that he had threatened them with punishment if they did not believe.

The words of the Most High: ﴿He said: "Indeed, Allah will bring it upon you, if He wills"﴾. He means: with the punishment. And His words: ﴿and you cannot escape﴾, meaning: you will not be able to outrun Him, nor flee.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 34:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And my counsel will not benefit you﴾. Al-nuṣḥ (sincere counsel) is: making one's action sincere, free from corruption. It was also said: it is the clarification of the place of error so that one may avoid it, and the clarification of the place of guidance so that one may seek it. His saying: ﴿If I desire to counsel you﴾ means: I desire conformity with the command of God. His saying: ﴿If God desires to lead you astray﴾ — most of the exegetes hold that its meaning is: to misguide you. It was also said: He creates error in your hearts, and error (al-ghayy) is the opposite of right guidance (al-rushd). Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari mentioned that the meaning of His saying ﴿to lead you astray﴾ is: to destroy you. Ibn al-Anbari did not accept this from the standpoint of the language, and said: it is not correct in the language that al-ighwa' be mentioned with the meaning of destruction. Some of them said: He will deprive you of His mercy.

His saying: ﴿He is your Lord, and to Him you will be returned﴾ — its meaning is evident, and in the verse there is a refutation of the Qadariyya.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 35:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"?﴾ Rather, they say, "He has invented it," meaning: he fabricated it. And His saying: ﴿Say, "If I have invented it, then upon me is my crime."﴾ It was recited in the irregular reading (shadh): "qa'alayya ajrami" with a fatha, and al-ajram is the plural of al-jurm, and al-ijram is the earning of sin. The meaning of the verse: upon me is the consequence of my sin and my crime. And His saying: ﴿And I am free of what you commit as crime﴾ means: I am free of what you earn of sin.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 36:

The words of the Most High: ﴿And it was revealed to Nuh﴾. Al-Dahhak narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that the people of Nuh used to beat Nuh until he fell, and they would throw him in a felt cloth and cast him into his house, thinking that he had died. Then he would come out on the next day and call them to Allah. It is narrated that an old man came leaning on a staff, and with him was his son, and he said: "O my son, do not let this old man, the madman, deceive you." So [Nuh] said: "O father, give me the staff." He handed him the staff, and he struck Nuh on his head and inflicted a grievous wound, so that blood flowed from him, while he was calling them to faith. Then Allah the Most High revealed: ﴿Indeed, none of your people will believe except those who have already believed﴾. Then he sought refuge in supplication and said: ﴿My Lord, do not leave upon the earth any of the disbelievers as a dweller﴾.

As for His words: ﴿So do not be distressed by what they have been doing﴾, Mujahid and Qatadah said: "So do not grieve." The lexicographers said: al-ibtila' (distress) is grief accompanied by submission. The poet said:

(Whatever Allah apportions, accept it without being dejected by it, and remain noble, of comfortable state.)

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 37:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And construct the ark under Our eyes﴾. It is reported from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "In Our sight."

And it is reported from al-Dahhak: "Under Our gaze." It was also said: "With Our seeing and Our protection." In the narrative: Jibril, upon him be peace, came to Nuh, upon him be peace, and said: "Your Lord commands you to construct the ark." He said: "How shall I construct it, when I am not a carpenter?" He said: "Your Lord says: Construct the ark, for you are under My eye." So he took the adze and began to construct the ark, and he did not miss a single spot.

And His saying: ﴿And by Our inspiration﴾, meaning: by Our command. And His saying: ﴿And do not address Me concerning those who have wronged; indeed, they are to be drowned﴾. Regarding this there are two opinions:

One of them: "Do not address Me concerning the reprieve of the disbelievers, for I have decreed their drowning."

The second: "Do not address Me concerning your son, for he is destined to perish with the people."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 38:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And he was constructing the ark﴾. It is narrated from Zayd ibn Aslam that he said: Nuh remained for a hundred years planting trees and cutting them, and he remained for a hundred years making the ark. And from Ka'b al-Ahbar (Ka'b al-Ahbar) that he said: Nuh built the ship over thirty years. And it is narrated from Salman al-Farisi that Nuh built the ship over four hundred years. This is mentioned in some tafsir works, but the well-known view is the first.

And His saying: ﴿And whenever a group of his people passed by him, they mocked him﴾. The people of tafsir said: Whenever they passed by him, they would say: "This man who used to claim that he is a prophet has become a carpenter."

It is also narrated that they used to say to him: "O Nuh, what are you making?" And he would say: "I am making a house that will walk on the water." So they would laugh at him and marvel at him.

In some tafsir works, it is related from Ibn 'Abbas that they had never seen a sea or a ship; rather, the seas today are remnants of the Flood.

And His saying: ﴿He said: "If you mock us, then we mock you just as you mock﴾. If it is said: How is it permissible for a prophet among the prophets to mock his own people?

The answer: This is in the form of a balanced rhetorical correspondence ( izdiwaj al-kalam), and its meaning is: If you consider me foolish, then I consider you foolish when the punishment descends. It was also said that its meaning is: If you mock me, then you will see the outcome of your mockery.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 39:

The Almighty's saying: ﴿So you will come to know who will receive a punishment that disgraces him﴾. This is connected to His saying: ﴿So you will come to know﴾. Its meaning is: "So you will come to know which of us ﴿will receive a punishment that disgraces him﴾." It was also said: "So you will come to know the one to whom there comes a punishment that disgraces him." This is the meaning of "yukhzihi" (disgraces him): it means "yuhlikuhu" (destroys him). It was also said: it means "yudhillahu" (humiliates him). His saying ﴿and an enduring punishment will descend upon him﴾ means: a lasting punishment will descend upon him, and it is the drowning.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 40:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿until when Our command came and the oven gushed forth⟩. The scholars differed concerning the "oven" (tannur), giving several opinions. The majority hold that it is the baker's oven; this is the view of Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, and a group.

It is related from 'Ikrimah that he said: it is the surface of the earth. This is also reported from Ibn 'Abbas. They said: it is as if God, exalted is He, set a sign between Him and Noah, saying: "When you see the water gushing forth over the surface of the earth, then board the ship."

The third opinion: what is related from 'Ali, may God be pleased with him, that he said: "wa fara al-tannur" means: the dawn broke open (infajara al-subh); and this is from their saying nawwara al-subh tanwiran (the dawn shone forth). Some said: the tannur here is a stone oven in which Eve used to bake, which Noah inherited, and God, exalted is He, said to Noah: "When the water gushes forth from the furthest place in your house, that is the sign." The word tannur is a word on which Arabic and Persian (al-ajamiyyah) agree.

The scholars differed concerning the location of the tannur:

It is related from 'Ali, may God be pleased with him, that he said: it was in Kufa, and he pointed toward the gate of Kindah to the mosque. Similarly, al-Sha'bi reported that the tannur gushed forth from the right side of the mosque of Kufa. It is related that a man came to 'Ali, may God be pleased with him, and said: "O Commander of the Faithful, I have bought a riding beast and prepared provisions to go and pray in the Mosque of Jerusalem." He said: "Sell your mount, eat your provisions, and pray in this mosque" – meaning the mosque of Kufa – "for seventy prophets prayed in it, and from it the tannur gushed forth."

Some said: the tannur was in Syria. Some said it was in the land of India.

Some said: the tannur was a spring in al-Jazirah called 'Ayn al-Wardah.

As for His saying: ﴿We said: Load therein of every pair two⟩, the pronoun "therein" refers to the ship (al-fulk). The scholars differed concerning the size of the ship:

It is related from al-Hasan al-Basri that he said: the length of the ship was twelve hundred cubits, and its breadth six hundred cubits. The well-known view is that its length was three hundred cubits, its breadth fifty cubits, and its height to the sky thirty cubits; and other things have been said, and God knows best.

Qatadah said: its door was in its width. They said: it had three decks: the upper deck for the birds, the lower deck for the predators and wild beasts, and the middle for men and women; and the partition between the women and the men was the body of Adam, for he was carried with himself in the ship.

As for His saying: ﴿of every pair two⟩, "zawj" is each one that does not dispense with its like; one says "a pair of shoes" (zawj khuff) and "a pair of sandals" (zawj na'l). What is meant by "the two of the pair" here is the male and the female; its meaning is: two of every male and female.

In the narrative: Noah, peace be upon him, said: "O Lord, how shall I carry two of every pair?" So God, exalted is He, gathered the predators and birds to him, and he began to strike with his hands at each kind, so the male would fall into his right hand and the female into his left, and he would carry them in the ship. Wahb ibn Munabbih mentioned that people complained to Noah about mice in the ship, so God, exalted is He, commanded him to wipe the forehead of the lion, and two cats came out of its nostrils and ate the mice; and they also complained to him about the abundance of dung, so he was commanded to wipe the rear of the elephant, and two boars came out of it and ate the dung.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿and your family⟩ means: carry your family ﴿except him against whom the word has already preceded⟩, meaning: his son and his wife. His saying: ﴿and those who believe⟩ means: and carry those who believe.

His saying: ﴿and none believed with him except a few⟩: they differed concerning their number. It is related from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: they were eighty persons. Others said: they were seventy-two persons. Al-A'mash said: they were seven persons: three sons of Noah, namely Sam, Ham, and Japheth, and their three wives – meaning their women – and Noah. Qatadah said: they were eight persons.

The commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Qur'an) on surah 11, verse 41:

His words, may He be exalted: ﴿And he said, "Embark therein; in the name of Allah is its sailing and its anchoring."﴾ [with both mīms read with fatḥa, mujrīhā and mursāhā]. Abu Raja' al-Utaridi read "mujrīhā wa mursīhā" with ḍamma (raf').

As for the meaning of His words ﴿mujrīhā wa mursāhā﴾, it means: "In the name of Allah is its (i.e., the ship's) causing to run (ijrā') and its causing to anchor (irsā')." And the meaning of "mujrīhā wa mursāhā" with naṣb is: "In the name of Allah is its running (jaryuhā) and its anchoring (rasuwwuhā)." Some of them said: When Noah said "In the name of Allah" and intended the running, it ran; and when he said "In the name of Allah" and intended the anchoring, it anchored.

As for the duration of Noah's stay in the ship, they said: The ship set off on the surface of the water on the tenth of Rajab, and it sailed for one hundred and fifty days, and it anchored on the tenth of Dhu al-Hijjah, and they descended to the earth on the day of ʿĀshūrāʾ. He fasted that day and commanded the people to fast it.

It is related in the stories (al-qaṣaṣ) that the ship circled the entire world, and when it reached the Kaʿba it circled around it for a week, and the Kaʿba had been raised while the site remained.

As for His words, ﴿Indeed, my Lord is Forgiving, Merciful﴾, its meaning is clear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 42:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And it sailed with them through waves like mountains﴾. The meaning of mawj (wave) is a piece of the sea that rises when the wind is very strong.

And His saying: ﴿And Noah called out to his son, and he was in a separate place﴾. It was said: in a separate place from the ship; and it was said: in a separate place from his people.

And His saying: ﴿O my son, board with us﴾. It was recited with two readings: "Yā bunayya" and "Yābunay," and their meaning is one. And His saying: ﴿and do not be with the disbelievers﴾, meaning: be not among the disbelievers. Its meaning is clear.

They differed as to whether he was his son by his loins (sulb) or not.

It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, and ʿIkrimah, Saʿid ibn Jubayr, al-Dahhak, and a group, that they said: he was his son by his loins. Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: "No wife of a prophet ever committed adultery." ʿIkrimah used to swear that he was truly the son of Noah by his loins. As for al-Hasan and Mujahid, they said: he was the son of his wife, and was not his son, and they relied on His saying, may He be glorified and exalted: ﴿So do not ask Me about that of which you have no knowledge﴾. They said: he (Noah) thought he was his son, but he was not his son. The first view is the most sound. It was said: his name was Kanʿan. It was said: his name was "Yam."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 43:

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿He said, "I will take refuge on a mountain that will protect me from the water."﴾ That is, "I will seek refuge at the mountain, which will keep me from drowning." Then Noah said to him: ﴿"There is no protector today from the command of Allah, except for the one on whom He has mercy."﴾ Regarding this there are two opinions:

The first: the protector (ʿāṣim) has the meaning of the one protected (maʿṣūm), and its meaning is: there is no one protected today from the command of Allah except the one on whom He has mercy.

The second opinion: "There is no protector today from the command of Allah except Allah."

His statement, exalted is He: ﴿except the one on whom He has mercy﴾ refers to Allah, exalted is He. And His statement ﴿And the wave came between them, so he was among the drowned﴾ means: he became among the drowned.

It is related in the account that the water rose over the mountain tops by a measure of forty cubits. It was also said: less than that. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 44:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And it was said: O earth, swallow your water﴾. Its meaning: drink up your water. It is also said: "ub'lai" means: conceal your water within your belly. His saying: ﴿And O sky, withhold﴾, meaning: hold back. His saying: ﴿And the water was diminished and the matter was decided﴾, meaning: the water decreased and dried up. His saying: ﴿And the matter was decided﴾, meaning: the affair was completed, which is the destruction of the people. His saying: ﴿And it came to rest upon al-Judi﴾, meaning: it settled upon al-Judi. It is said that it is a mountain in the region of Amid. Al-Farra' said: a mountain in the region of Nasibin. His saying: ﴿And it was said: Away with the wrongdoing people﴾, meaning: destruction for the wrongdoing people.

In the codex of Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him: "And the water was diminished, and it came to rest upon al-Judi, and the matter was decided."

It is narrated that Noah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, sent out the raven to bring him news of the earth, but it settled on a carcass and did not return. So he sent out the dove, and it came back with an olive leaf in its beak and its feet smeared with mud, so that Noah would know that the water had subsided. From that time the dove was given the collar [and the reddening] of the legs.

This verse is counted among the most eloquent verses of the Qur'an, and it is related that when it was recited in the presence of a Bedouin, he said: "This is the speech of One who is capable."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 45:

His, the Exalted and Glorified's, saying: ﴿And Noah called out to his Lord and said, "My Lord, indeed my son is of my family, and indeed Your promise is true, and You are the most just of judges."﴾ That is: You promised me that You would save my family, and You are the most just of judges, meaning: You are the most just of judges in justice.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿O Noah, indeed he is not of your family﴾. Its meaning: he is not of your family whom I promised you that I would save. According to the opinion of al-Hasan and Mujahid, it means: he is not your son.

And His saying: ﴿indeed, he is one whose deeds are unrighteous﴾. Its meaning: indeed, he is one possessing unrighteous deeds.

The second opinion: your asking Me to save him is an unrighteous deed.

In the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, it is: "indeed, it is an unrighteous deed."

﴿So do not ask Me about that of which you have no knowledge﴾. This supports the second meaning. It has also been recited as: "indeed, it is an unrighteous deed," and its meaning is: indeed, your son is an unrighteous deed.

As for His saying, the Exalted: ﴿So do not ask Me about that of which you have no knowledge﴾, there are two opinions concerning it:

One of them: Noah used to think that he was a Muslim while he was concealing disbelief inherited from his father. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿Do not ask Me about that of which you have no knowledge﴾.

The second: its meaning is that he is not your son, as we have mentioned.

As for His saying: ﴿I admonish you lest you be among the ignorant﴾, its meaning: I warn you lest you be among the sinners. The sin of the believer is ignorance, and the sin of the disbeliever is disbelief.

The second opinion: ﴿I admonish you lest you be among the ignorant﴾ — meaning: lest you ask for the destruction of the disbelievers and then seek the salvation of a disbeliever.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 47:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He said﴾, that is, Noah said: ﴿My Lord, I seek refuge in You from asking You﴾

Rather, I refrain (amtani') through You from asking You ﴿about that of which I have no knowledge﴾. Its meaning: the request for protection (ʿiṣmah).

And His saying: ﴿And unless You forgive me and have mercy on me, I will be among the losers﴾ — its meaning is apparent.

"It was said: 'O Noah, descend with peace from Us.'" Its meaning: descend in safety, from Us.

And His words, "and blessings upon you." Blessing (barakah) is the establishment of goodness, and from it comes the kneeling of the camel (buruk al-ba'ir). It was also said: the blessing here is that Allah, glorified and exalted, made him the "second Adam" (Adam al-asghar), so He destroyed all who were with him without offspring, and made the offspring from his progeny continue until the Hour.

And His words, "and upon nations from among those with you." Its meaning: upon the descendants of nations from among those with you. Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: everyone who believes until the Hour entered into it, being in the loins of Noah.

His words, "And nations We shall provide for, then a painful punishment will touch them from Us" — this is the beginning of a new statement, and its meaning: and nations We shall provide for, and they are the disbelievers. His words, "then a painful punishment will touch them from Us," the meaning is clear.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 49:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿That is among the tidings of the unseen, which We reveal to you﴾, meaning: We cast it to you. His saying: ﴿Neither you nor your people knew it before this﴾, meaning: before the sending down of the Qur'an. His saying: ﴿So be patient, for the good end is for the God-fearing﴾, the meaning is apparent.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 50:

The Almighty's saying: ﴿And to ʿĀd (We sent) their brother Hūd﴾. ʿĀd were a people who dwelt in al-Aḥqāf, which are sand dunes between Yemen and the Levant (al-Shām). It is also said that they dwelt in Yemen itself, and that they had been given an increase in stature and strength over all other creatures. His saying: ﴿their brother﴾ means their brother in lineage, not in religion. The meaning of the verse: "And We sent to ʿĀd their brother Hūd."

His saying: ﴿He said: O my people, worship Allah﴾, that is, make Allah one (waḥḥidū Allāh). His saying: ﴿You have no god other than Him. You are but fabricators﴾. Al-Iftirāʾ (fabrication) is lying, and their lying was against Allah, the Exalted.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 51:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O my people, I do not ask you for any wage for it﴾, meaning: a reward, i.e., I do not ask you for a wage for conveying the message. And His saying: ﴿My reward is only from the One who originated me﴾, its meaning: my reward is only from the One who originated me, i.e., created me. ﴿Will you not then reflect?﴾ The meaning is clear.

"And O my people, seek forgiveness from your Lord and then turn to Him in repentance." He placed seeking forgiveness before repentance because of the meaning we have explained.

As for His saying: "He will send down the sky upon you in abundance" (yursil al-sama' 'alaykum midrara), its meaning is: He will send the sky upon you with rain abundantly, time after time, at times of need. The word midrar is used in the form of intensification (mubalagha), as one says: "a woman who is mi'tar and midhkar" (a woman who frequently bears children, and a woman who frequently bears males).

As for His saying: "and add strength to your strength" (wa yazidkum quwwatan ila quwwatikum): it is reported that God withheld the rain from them for three years and rendered the wombs of the mothers barren, so they did not give birth. The meaning of His saying "and add strength to your strength" is: He will send the rain upon you, and you will increase in wealth, and He will restore the wombs of the mothers to what they were, so they will give birth, and you will increase in strength through wealth and children. It has also been said that "and add strength to your strength" means: intensity to your intensity. And it has been said: "add to you strength in your religion to your strength in your bodies."

As for His saying: "and do not turn away as criminals" (wa la tatawallaw mujrimin), it means: and do not turn away.

"The Exalted's saying: ﴿They said, "O Hud, you have brought us no clear proof"﴾, that is, no evident argument. And His saying: ﴿and we will not abandon our gods on your word﴾, that is, because of your saying. ﴿And we are not going to believe you﴾, that is, we will not accept you as truthful."

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verses 54–55:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿We only say that some of our gods have struck you with evil﴾ means: "only afflicted you." The poet said:

(I came to you naked, my clothes worn, out of fear, as you suspect me of suspicions.)

The "naked" (ʿārī) here is the one who asks; he is called "naked" because he seeks to be afflicted (by the hardship of need).

And His saying: ﴿with some evil﴾ means: with madness (lamm) and derangement (khabl). It is as if they said: "You insulted our gods, so they have taken revenge on you by deranging you and afflicting you with madness." And His saying: ﴿He said: "Indeed I call Allah to witness, and you bear witness that I am free from what you associate, apart from Him"﴾. If it is asked: how did he say to the polytheists, "and bear witness," when they have no testimony? We say: this is mentioned as a way of emphasising the proof, not as a way of affirming that they have any testimony.

And His saying: ﴿So scheme against me all together, then give me no respite﴾. Kayd (scheming) is the contrivance of a human being. This statement is a miracle for Hud, peace be upon him, for he commanded them to devise every stratagem to bring harm upon him, and Allah, exalted is He, prevented them from that, so they were not able to do it. This is similar to the saying of Noah in Surah Yunus: ﴿So resolve upon your affair and your partners, then let not your affair be obscure to you; then carry it out against me and give me no respite﴾. We have already explained its interpretation.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verses 54–55:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿We only say that some of our gods have struck you with evil﴾ means: "only afflicted you." The poet said:

(I came to you naked, my clothes worn, out of fear, as you suspect me of suspicions.)

The "naked" (ʿārī) here is the one who asks; he is called "naked" because he seeks to be afflicted (by the hardship of need).

And His saying: ﴿with some evil﴾ means: with madness (lamm) and derangement (khabl). It is as if they said: "You insulted our gods, so they have taken revenge on you by deranging you and afflicting you with madness." And His saying: ﴿He said: "Indeed I call Allah to witness, and you bear witness that I am free from what you associate, apart from Him"﴾. If it is asked: how did he say to the polytheists, "and bear witness," when they have no testimony? We say: this is mentioned as a way of emphasising the proof, not as a way of affirming that they have any testimony.

And His saying: ﴿So scheme against me all together, then give me no respite﴾. Kayd (scheming) is the contrivance of a human being. This statement is a miracle for Hud, peace be upon him, for he commanded them to devise every stratagem to bring harm upon him, and Allah, exalted is He, prevented them from that, so they were not able to do it. This is similar to the saying of Noah in Surah Yunus: ﴿So resolve upon your affair and your partners, then let not your affair be obscure to you; then carry it out against me and give me no respite﴾. We have already explained its interpretation.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 56:

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, I have relied upon Allah, my Lord and your Lord.﴾ Its meaning: I have depended upon Allah, my Lord and your Lord. And His saying: ﴿There is no creature but that He holds its forelock.﴾ Its meaning: there is no creature but that it is in His grip, and His power reaches it. He singled out the forelock (nasiyah) for mention because humiliation and subjugation are in seizing the forelock.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, my Lord is on a straight path.﴾ Concerning it there are several opinions:

The first: its meaning is that my Lord acts with justice, and although He is capable of everything, He does not act except with benevolence and justice.

The second: ﴿Indeed, my Lord is on a straight path⦄ means: indeed, the religion of my Lord is on a straight path.

The third: His saying ﴿Indeed, my Lord is on a straight path﴾ has the same meaning as His saying: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is ever watchful⦄ (al-mirsad), meaning: He is upon the way of all creation.

The Qur'anic quotations are rendered with the ﴿ ﴾ markers kept, and the commentary is translated as it stands.

God the Exalted's words: ﴿And if they turn away, then I have conveyed to you what I was sent with to you﴾. Its meaning: if they turn away, then I have conveyed to you what I was sent with to you. And His words: ﴿And my Lord will replace you with another people﴾. Its meaning: if you turn away, He will destroy you and replace you with another people who are more obedient to God than you. And His words ﴿and you will not harm Him at all﴾: meaning, you will not diminish Him at all. And His words: ﴿Indeed, my Lord is Guardian over all things﴾: that is, Preserver of the affairs of His creation, according to what He has arranged and decreed.

"The saying of the Exalted: ﴿And when Our command came, We saved Hud and those who believed with him﴾ — the verse. His saying: ﴿Our command﴾, i.e., Our punishment. ﴿We saved Hud and those who believed with him by a mercy from Us﴾, i.e., by the fact that We guided them and made clear to them the path of guidance until they believed. And His saying: ﴿and We saved them from a harsh punishment﴾. The harsh punishment is the punishment with which He destroyed ʿAd and their people, and it was the al-rīḥ al-ʿaqīm (the barren wind). The wind would enter into their nostrils and mouths and exit from their posteriors, cutting them into pieces, i.e., piece by piece."

And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And that was ʿĀd; they denied the signs of their Lord﴾. Its meaning: they rejected the signs of their Lord. And His saying: ﴿and disobeyed His messengers﴾, i.e., by denying them. And His saying: ﴿and followed the command of every obstinate tyrant﴾. It was said: the jabbār (tyrant) is the one who kills in anger, and the ʿanīd (obstinate) is the one who opposes [the truth]. The poet said:

(Indeed I am an old man who cannot endure the ʿanad [stubbornness/rebellious camels],
and I cannot endure the shirdād [wild, skittish] young camels.)

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 60:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿And they were followed by a curse in this world﴾. Al-la'nah (curse) is distancing from mercy. The scholars said: It is not permissible to curse animals, because they do not deserve to be distanced from the mercy of Allah. It is established that a man cursed his camel during a journey, and the Prophet (ﷺ) ordered him to dismount from it and let it go, and said: "No cursed one shall accompany us." This is by way of rebuke and deterrence for the one who curses.

And His words: ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection, indeed 'Ad disbelieved their Lord﴾, meaning: they disbelieved in their Lord. And His words: ﴿Oh, away with 'Ad, the people of Hud!﴾ mean: Oh, far away with destruction, disgrace and ruin for 'Ad, the people of Hud.

And to Thamud, [We sent] their brother Salih. He said: "O my people, worship Allah; you have no deity other than Him." [Qur'an 11:61]

Its meaning: And We sent to Thamud their brother Salih. As for His saying "their brother," it is as we have mentioned earlier. Thamud were a people who lived in al-Hijr, between the Hijaz and al-Sham.

As for His saying: "He said: O my people, worship Allah," meaning: affirm the oneness of Allah (tawhid). "You have no deity other than Him," meaning: you have no object of worship other than Him.

As for His saying: "He produced you from the earth," there are two views on it:

One: He produced you in the earth. The other, which is: He produced you from the earth, because He created them from Adam, and Adam was created from the earth.

As for His saying: "and settled you in it," there are two views on it:

One: He lengthened your lives in it, and one of them would live from three hundred years up to a thousand years; and likewise the people of 'Ad.

The second view: He made you inhabitants (u'mmar) of it, by building dwellings and planting trees. This was reported by al-Farra' and al-Zajjaj.

As for His saying: "So seek His forgiveness, then turn to Him in repentance," the meaning has already been explained. As for His saying: "Indeed my Lord is near, responsive," near to the believers, responsive to their supplication.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 62:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿They said, "O Salih, you were among us a man of hope before this.﴾ That is: we used to hope good would come from you, but now we have despaired of your good and your success. And His saying: ﴿Do you forbid us to worship what our fathers worshipped?﴾ its meaning is clear. And His saying: ﴿Indeed, we are in disquiet﴾ in doubt (shakk, ريب) ﴿about that to which you invite us, [and] in suspicion﴾ that is, in doubt (murtab, مرتاب). And this is by way of emphasis.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 63:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿He said, "O my people, have you considered: if I am upon clear evidence from my Lord"﴾, meaning: upon proof from my Lord. And His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿and He has given me mercy from Himself﴾, "mercy" here means prophethood.

And His saying: ﴿so who will support me against Allah if I disobey Him?﴾, meaning: who will prevent from me the punishment of Allah if I disobey Him.

And His saying: ﴿so you add nothing to me but loss﴾, concerning which there are two opinions:

The first: if I follow you, I would be only like one who increases in loss and perdition.

The second opinion: "so you add nothing to me but loss" for yourselves. Its real meaning is: I seek from you guidance, while you give me loss and perdition, meaning: for your own selves.

All of this is an answer to the question of one who asked concerning this verse: how did he say ﴿so you add nothing to me but loss﴾ when he was not in loss?

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 64:

And His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And O my people, this is the she-camel of Allah, as a sign for you﴾. It is related that his people asked him to bring forth a pregnant she-camel from this solid rock, and they pointed to a rock in front of them. He said: So Salih supplicated his Lord, and the rock writhed (tamakhkhadat), and a moaning was heard from it like the moaning of a she-camel. Then there came forth from it a she-camel, the greatest that a she-camel could be, and she gave birth immediately to a young one like her. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿This is the she-camel of Allah, as a sign for you﴾.

And His saying: ﴿So leave her to feed on Allah's earth﴾, meaning: leave her to feed on Allah's earth. And His saying: ﴿And do not touch her with harm﴾, meaning: by destroying her. And His saying: ﴿Lest a near punishment seize you﴾, its meaning: near to the destruction of the she-camel.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 65:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So they hamstrung her﴾. Al-'Aqr (hamstringing) here means a wound that leads to death.

And His saying ﴿He said: "Enjoy yourselves in your homes"﴾. Its meaning: live in your homes. The word "dar" (home) here carries the sense of "diyar" (dwellings).

And His saying: ﴿"For three days. That is a promise not to be denied."﴾ It is narrated that he said to them: "The punishment will come upon you after three days. On the first day you will wake up with your faces yellow, then on the second day you will wake up with your faces red, then on the third day you will wake up with your faces black." So it happened as he said, and the punishment came upon them on the fourth day.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 66:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿So when Our command came, We saved Salih and those who believed with him by a mercy from Us﴾. In some tafsirs it is related that four thousand men believed with him. His saying: ﴿And from the disgrace of that day﴾ means: and from the destruction of that day. His saying: ﴿Indeed, your Lord is the Strong, the Mighty﴾ — we have already explained the meaning of al-Qawiyy (the Strong) and al-Aziz (the Mighty) earlier.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 67:

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And those who had done wrong were seized by the Blast﴾. It is well known that Jibril (Gabriel) cried out at them with a single cry, and they all perished to the last one. Some of them said: God, exalted is He, created a cry within the body of some animals, and it destroyed them. If it is said: "al-sayha (the Blast)" is feminine, and yet He said: ﴿And those who had done wrong were seized by the Blast﴾?

The answer to this: al-sayha here means al-siyah (the cry), and this is permissible in the language.

As for His saying: ﴿So they were found lying prostrate in their homes﴾, that is: dead. It is said: they fell upon their faces, dead, to the last one. From this comes "jatham al-ta'ir" (the bird settled and remained still). And from this is the report transmitted: "He forbade the mujaththamah" (the animal tied up and shot or left to die as a target).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 68:

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿As though they had never dwelt therein in ease﴾. Its meaning: as though they had never resided there in comfort and happiness.

And His saying: ﴿Indeed, Thamud disbelieved in their Lord﴾, i.e., disbelieved in their Lord. And His saying: ﴿Then away with Thamud!﴾ Its meaning is as we have mentioned before.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 69:

The Almighty's saying: ﴿And Our messengers came to Abraham with the good news﴾. Al-Suddi said: "They were twelve angels." Others said: "They were nine of the angels."

It is also said: "They were three: Jibril (Gabriel), Mika'il (Michael), and Israfil (Israfil)." And it was said: "They came in the form of men."

In the narrative: Abraham, may the blessings of God be upon him, would not eat except with a guest, and he remained fifteen nights without a guest coming to him. Then these angels came to him. As for His saying ﴿with the good news﴾, there are two views:

The first: the good news of Isaac. The second: the good news of the destruction of the people of Lot.

As for His saying ﴿They said, "Peace"﴾, its meaning is: they said, "We greet you with peace." ﴿He said, "Peace"﴾ has been read in two ways: the first is "Salam" (سَلَام), which is the well-known reading, and the second is "Salm" (سَلْم), the reading of Hamza and al-Kisa'i. As for His saying ﴿Peace﴾, its meaning is: my reply is "peace," or my word is "peace." As for the reading "Salm," it has been said that al-Silm and al-Salam have the same meaning, like al-Hill and al-Halal, and al-Haram and al-Haram. It is also said that "al-Silm" means reconciliation, so its meaning is: "I seek safety from you."

As for His saying ﴿Then he did not delay, but brought a roasted calf﴾, this is evidence that a guest should be hastened to with something to eat, and it is the sunnah of Abraham, may the blessings of God be upon him. As for His saying ﴿brought a roasted calf﴾: "al-'Ijl" is the young of a cow, and "al-Hanid" is the same as "al-mahnud," which is that which is roasted on heated stones; a trench is dug for it in the ground and it is roasted in it. It is related that it was fat, dripping with grease.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 70:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿When he saw their hands not reaching toward it﴾, meaning: when he saw that they were not eating, for the angels do not eat. His saying: ﴿nakirahum﴾ means: he disliked them (ankarahum), as the poet said:

(Fa-ankartani wa-ma kana alladhi nakirtu ... min al-hawadith illa al-shayba wa-al-salʿa)

[She] failed to recognize me, and what I failed to recognize among the calamities was nothing but the grey hair and the baldness.

His saying: ﴿And he felt a fear of them﴾: Ibrahim, peace be upon him, was staying at the edge of the people's settlement. When these men entered upon him and did not eat, he feared that they had come with a calamity and an intent to harm. It was the custom of the Arabs that when people eat of a person's food, they become safe from him, and when they do not eat, they feel fear. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And he felt a fear of them﴾. His saying: ﴿Awjas﴾ means: he concealed within himself a fear of them. His saying: ﴿They said, "Do not fear; we have been sent to the people of Lut"﴾ means: We are angels, whom our Lord has sent to the people of Lut.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 71:

And His saying: ﴿And his wife was standing﴾. In the codex of Ibn Mas'ud it reads: "And his wife was standing, and he was seated." She was Sarah, daughter of Haran. It is said that Sarah was serving them while Ibrahim was conversing with them. It is also said that Sarah was standing behind the screen.

His saying: ﴿so she laughed﴾. Most scholars hold that the laughter here is the well-known laughter. Mujahid and Ikrimah said: "so she laughed" means she menstruated; it is said, "the female hare laughed" when she menstruated.

As for the well-known laughter, scholars differ over why she laughed.

Most of them hold that she laughed out of joy at the removal of fear from her and from Ibrahim. It is also said that she laughed at the good news of Ishaq. According to this view, the verse is in inverted order: it is as if He said: "And his wife was standing, so We gave her the good news of Ishaq, and after Ishaq, Ya'qub, and she laughed."

The third view: she laughed in wonder at the heedlessness of the people of Lut, while the angels had come down with their punishment.

His saying ﴿So We gave her good news of Ishaq﴾ is clear in meaning. His saying ﴿and after Ishaq, Ya'qub﴾ means: after Ishaq, Ya'qub. Abu 'Ubaydah said: "al-Waraa'" means the son's son.

His saying ﴿Ya'qub﴾ has been read in two ways: "Ya'qub" and "Ya'qub" (with different vowelling), in the nominative and the accusative. As for the nominative, its meaning is: Ya'qub will be born after Ishaq. As for the accusative, its meaning is: We gave her good news of Ishaq and We gave her good news of Ya'qub. A poet recited regarding al-Waraa':

(I swore, and I did not leave for you any doubt, and there is no refuge for a man beyond God.)

This is a verse of al-A'sha.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 72:

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿She said: "Woe to me! Shall I bear a child when I am an old woman and this, my husband, is an old man?"﴾ They (the scholars) said: The original form of ﴿Woe to me!﴾ is "yā wailatī" (يا ويلتي); except that here the alif has replaced the yā (in the word "yā wailatī", the alif is substituted for the yā). The meaning of ﴿Woe to me!﴾ here is: "How strange!" This is an expression that a person says upon seeing something that amazes him, and it is not meant in the literal sense of calling down woe.

As for His words, the Exalted: ﴿Shall I bear a child when I am an old woman﴾, the scholars differed regarding the ages of Ibrahim and Sarah at that time.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Ibrahim's age was one hundred and twenty years, and Sarah's age was ninety years. Some of them said: Ibrahim's age was one hundred years, and Sarah's age was ninety-nine years. Other views have been mentioned besides this, and Allah knows best.

As for His words, the Exalted: ﴿and this, my husband﴾, meaning: this is my husband. ﴿Old man (shaykhan)﴾ is in the accusative case as a circumstantial qualifier of detachment (ʿalā al-qaṭʿ, i.e., a qualifier that clarifies the state of the subject), and it was said: it is in the accusative as a state (ḥāl).

In the recitation of Ibn Mas'ud: "wa hādhā baʿlī shaykhun" (وَهَذَا بعلي شيخ), in the nominative as a predicate (khabar). As for His words, the Exalted: ﴿Indeed, this is a wondrous thing﴾, meaning: indeed, this is something astonishing, contrary to the usual custom.

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 73:

His saying: ﴿They said, "Are you amazed at the decree of Allah?"﴾ Its meaning: do not be amazed at the decree of Allah, for when Allah wills something, it is.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The mercy of Allah and His blessings be upon you, O people of the house﴾ has two meanings:

The first: that this is in the sense of supplication (du'a') from the angels.

The second: that it is in the sense of information (khabar), and ﴿the mercy of Allah﴾ means: the favour of Allah. ﴿And His blessings﴾: "barakat" is the plural of "barakah" (blessing), and "barakah" (blessing) is the establishment of good (thubut al-khayr). It was also said: "And His blessings" means: His felicities (sa'adat).

And His saying: ﴿upon you, O people of the house﴾ is evidence that the wives may be called "people of the house" (ahl al-bayt).

The Shi'a claimed, regarding His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Allah only intends to remove from you the uncleanness, O people of the house﴾, that the wives are not included in this. But this verse is evidence that they are included in it.

His saying: ﴿Indeed, He is Praiseworthy and Glorious﴾. Al-Hamid (the Praiseworthy) is the one praised in His actions, and al-Majid (the Glorious) is the Generous (al-Karim). The root of "majd" (glory) is elevation and nobility (al-raf'ah wa al-sharaf).

Commentary of al-Sam'ani (Tafsir al-Quran) on surah 11, verse 74:

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿When the fear had left Abraham﴾. Qatadah said: al-raw' (الروع) is fear (al-faza'). As for al-rawh (الروح) with a damma, it means the soul (al-nafs), and from it is his saying (ﷺ): "The Holy Spirit (Ruh al-Qudus) has inspired into my heart that no soul will die until it has completed its provision.
